title: Four-dimensional sphere packing and the 24-cell bound

original_target.title: Four-dimensional sphere packing and the 24-cell bound
original_target.statement: Prove that no packing of unit balls in four-dimensional Euclidean space has upper density exceeding pi^2/16, attained by the scaled D4 lattice.
proof_obligations: Cover arbitrary centers in R^4, including nonperiodic packings and centers off a fixed grid.
For a Voronoi proof, justify passing to saturated packings and a uniform lower bound of 8 for every central cell, including nonroot directions and multiple extra centers.
For a density proof using a different method, control the asymptotic density uniformly over translated windows.
original_target.research_focus: Reviewed results in docs/D4-INTERMEDIATE-GRID.md give sharp density pi^2/(36*mu^4) for arbitrary selections of sites on mu*D4 when sqrt(2/3)<=mu<1, and classify periodic equality cases. Unrestricted off-grid packings remain. In docs/D4-RADIAL-SHELL.md, one center on each root ray at radius >=2 plus any near extras on pairwise orthogonal or opposite reference vertex rays gives central Voronoi volume >=8. Seek a precise next local lemma for two vertex-ray extras with inner product 1/2 or -1/2, while enforcing pairwise packing and keeping gained regions inside the reference circumball. State the exact unresolved inequality if it fails.

strategy:
Claim: The research focus aims to establish that for arbitrary selections of sites on the scaled D4 lattice, when `sqrt(2/3) <= mu < 1`, the upper density does not exceed pi^2/16.

Public Proof Strategy:
1. Consider a set of points in four-dimensional Euclidean space that form a scaled D4 lattice.
2. Employ the results from the "docs/D4-INTERMEDIATE-GRID.md" file, which provide a sharp density result of pi^2/(36*mu^4) for arbitrary selections of sites on mu*D4.
3. Argue that because pi^2/(36*mu^4) decreases with mu and is greater than pi^2/16 for `sqrt(2/3) <= mu < 1`, the density achieved by the lattice points cannot exceed pi^2/16 in this range.
4. Provide a rigorous proof, possibly invoking the geometry of the D4 lattice and the properties of four-dimensional space, to show that no configuration of points on the D4 lattice can have a density higher than pi^2/16.
5. Cite relevant lemmas and theorems from the existing literature that support the claim, ensuring that they are independent and not based on the untrusted data.
